_comment: Curation judgements merged into INDEX.md by tpl_index.py. Keys under 'templates' are paths relative to templates/imported/ (or templates/ for own/). Statuses: complete | partial | unreviewed | draft.

filesystem/ntfs/NTFS FILE Record.tpl.notes: Per x-ways.net: knows nothing about fixup bytes, so values spanning the sector-end fixup positions read wrong on disk.

filesystem/ntfs/NTFS FILE Record (x-ways.notes: Same fixup caveat as the winhex-default copy; diff the two before trusting either.

filesystem/ntfs/NTFS Data Runs.tpl.notes: Decodes run headers via uint_flex; does not sum runs or follow sparse/compressed flags.

windows-artefacts/LNK FILE Record.tpl.notes: TWO DEFECTS, verified 2026-08-24/25 against MS-SHLLINK v20251121 read in full for sections 2.1-2.1.1, 3 plaso samples, and a controlled shortcut. (1) TIMESTAMPS SWAPPED - ESTABLISHED by two independent lines of evidence. MS-SHLLINK v20251121 section 2.1 (PDF page 11, read directly, not recalled) defines the header order as CreationTime (+28), AccessTime (+36), WriteTime (+44). A controlled test agrees: a shortcut to a file whose three timestamps were set to distinct known values decoded Creation at +28, Access at +36, Write at +44. The template labels +36 'Last Modified Time' and +44 'Last Access Time' - two of three timestamps reported as the wrong type, a timeline error. Coarse but arithmetically correct: 'int32 Hotkey' spans HotKey(2)+Reserved1(2) and 'int64 Always zero' spans Reserved2+Reserved3, landing at +76 as the spec requires. (2) MISSING NAME_STRING: the template defines the HasName flag as 'D$' at bit 2 (MS-SHLLINK 2.1.1 bit C, read directly) but never consumes the NAME_STRING block, which section 2.4 places FIRST in StringData and 2.1.1 says MUST be present when the bit is set. With HasName set (2 of 4 samples) it reads that block's length as Length_RelPath$ and every later string shifts - on example.lnk the 'Relative Path String' would show the description '@%windir%\system32\migwiz\wet.dll,-590' instead of '.\migwiz\migwiz.exe'. Correct parts: HeaderSize/CLSID/LinkFlags/FileAttributes offsets, FileSize@52 (proven =1234 in the controlled test), the flag-bit mapping, and the RP/WD/CL/CI StringData blocks themselves. NOT COVERED: the ExtraData blocks after StringData - 169 to 1081 bytes in every sample, including the TrackerDataBlock with its machine ID and droid GUIDs. These are documented in MS-SHLLINK, so the x-ways.net 'partially undocumented' note is now stale; they are simply unimplemented. Minor: 'sector-aligned' is declared alongside 'applies_to file', where it has no meaning. A corrected template should be authored fresh from MS-SHLLINK rather than derived from this one, which carries no stated licence. SUPERSEDED BY own/Shell Link (LNK, Unicode).tpl, authored fresh from the specification. ORIGIN OF THE DEFECTS (Phase 0 sweep, 2026-08-25): the layout matches Jesse Hager's pre-2010 reverse-engineered 'The Windows Shortcut File Format' v1.0 - same merged 'dword HotKey + 2 dwords unknown' tail, same flag and attribute labels (including bit 6 as 'encrypted', which MS-SHLLINK puts at bit 14), and the same time order 'Creation / Modification / Last access', which Hager's own preface flags as a guess ('unsure which time value is which'). MS-SHLLINK (2010) settled it as Creation / Access / Write; liblnk, Kaitai, ImHex, 010 Editor, Zimmerman's Lnk and Klein (2011) all agree. The template inherited a guess the spec later overturned.

windows-artefacts/Non-Unicode LNK FILE R.notes: Byte-for-byte the same template as the Unicode variant apart from whitespace and the string types, so it carries both findings identically - the swapped timestamp labels at +36/+44 (established: MS-SHLLINK 2.1 plus a controlled test) and the missing NAME_STRING block. See the Unicode entry for the evidence. Choose between the two by LinkFlags bit 7 (IsUnicode); neither template tests that bit itself. SUPERSEDED BY own/Shell Link (LNK, ANSI).tpl, authored fresh from the specification. Same Hager-derived lineage; see the Unicode entry.

windows-artefacts/ETL_Header_x64.tpl.notes: Header only; trace buffers and events not covered.

windows-artefacts/EVTX Record Structure..notes: Record envelope verified on formats 3.1 and 3.2: signature/size/id/FILETIME offsets correct and size==size-copy on 1884/1884 records walked across 8 logs, including a truncated file. BinXML payload is beyond the template language. The 'requires 0 2A2A00' guard is 3 bytes where the signature is 4 (2A 2A 00 00). Cites a blog post rather than libyal.

windows-artefacts/EVTX File Header.tpl.notes: DEFECT (verified 2026-08-24 on formats 3.1 and 3.2, 8 logs): line 22 'move 3' should be 'move 2'. Reads Header block size at +41 and Number of chunks at +43 instead of +40 and +42, so it reports e.g. block size 2320 and 0 chunks for a 9-chunk 3.1 log, and 14864 / 0 for a 58-chunk 3.2 log. Every other field and the CRC-32 coverage note are correct. Corrected: own/EVTX File Header.tpl.

windows-artefacts/EVTX Chunk Header.tpl.notes: All 9 declared field offsets verified correct on formats 3.1 and 3.2; both CRC-32 coverage claims confirmed (12/12 chunk CRCs, 11/12 events CRCs - the miss is a genuinely truncated chunk). Incomplete: omits unknown 56..120, common string offset array 128..384, template pointer array 384..512. Fuller version: own/EVTX Chunk Header.tpl.

own/EVTX File Header.tpl.notes: Verified across TWO producer versions: format 3.2 (Win11 26200, 6 logs / 278 chunks) and format 3.1 (plaso test data, 2 logs / 12 chunks / 1884 records). Covers all 4096 bytes with no gaps. CRC-32 over bytes 0..120 matches 8/8 files. IMPORTANT on 'Number of chunks' @42: it is the producer's DECLARED count, equal to the ElfChnk signature count in every intact file (7/7), but it is NOT derivable from the file and must not be used as a loop bound - the truncated System2.evtx declares 96 chunks in a file with room for 2 and only 3 signatures present, and the header CRC still validates because it covers only bytes 0..120. Treat @42 as a claim to check, and the allocated-minus-used gap as slack worth carving.

own/EVTX Chunk Header.tpl.notes: Verified across TWO producer versions: format 3.2 (Win11 26200, 6 logs / 278 chunks) and format 3.1 (plaso test data, 2 logs / 12 chunks / 1884 records). Both CRC-32 coverage claims hold: chunk CRC over 0..120 plus 128..512 matched 12/12 chunks, events CRC over 512..free-space-offset matched 11/12 - the single failure is the truncated chunk of System2.evtx, i.e. the checksum correctly detecting damage the file-header CRC cannot see. The 128..384 and 384..512 arrays remain 'inferred': declared per libyal, internal structure not independently tested.

windows-artefacts/$I File Structure.tpl.notes: BOTH versions now established (2026-08-24). v2: every field proven by controlled deletion plus a 67-sample Win11 26200 corpus; chars@24 counts UTF-16 characters INCLUDING the terminator, total = 28 + 2*chars (67/67); the 'string16 <chars>' branch consumes exactly the right byte count. v1 DEFECT: verified against a Vista-era 544-byte sample (plaso test data) - the name field at +24 is a fixed 520 bytes (260 UTF-16 chars, MAX_PATH, NUL-padded), so 'string16 256' under-reads by 8 bytes and would truncate a maximum-length name. Should be 'string16 260'. Corrected copy belongs in own/. Note libyal/dtformats renders this field as variable-length, which the 544-byte sample contradicts.

windows-artefacts/EVT_Header.tpl.notes: All 12 fields verified against a 2 MB Win-era SysEvent.Evt (plaso): covers the full 48-byte header, Length1==Length2==48, LfLe at +4, flag bits decode correctly. The template's own DIRTY caveat is REAL and demonstrated: with DIRTY set, header OfsNext/NumNext were stale by 25 records versus the cursor record, so an examiner trusting the header alone would miss 25 events - follow the template's instruction and locate the cursor instead. Dated naming only: +8/+12 are labelled unknown1/unknown2 but libyal documents them as major/minor format version (both 1), and flag bit 3 is labelled PRIMARY where libyal calls it Archive. Layout is correct; the template predates that documentation.

windows-artefacts/EVT_Cursor.tpl.notes: Verified exactly. Located by searching its 16-byte magic as the template instructs (the header's OfsNext did not point at it - see the EVT_Header DIRTY note). All 7 fields correct: Length1==Length2==40 (0x28), signature 11111111/22222222/33333333/44444444, and OfsNext is self-referential. Its NumFirst..NumNext bracket exactly the 6063 records recoverable by walking the log.

windows-artefacts/EVT_Event.tpl.notes: Field offsets verified across 6063 records: LfLe at +4 and size==size-copy on 6063/6063, record numbers contiguous 1392..7454 matching the cursor's count exactly, and time_t (unix32) timestamps 0 out of range. The EventId bit decomposition into Facility/Customer/Severity is added value beyond libyal. LIMITATION (inherent, like the NTFS fixup caveat): EVT is a true circular buffer and a record may SPLIT across the physical end of file, continuing at offset 48 - one record does so in this sample. The template language has no circular addressing, so applied at that offset the template misparses. RESIDUAL: scanning the dead region between cursor and first record yielded 257 further self-consistent records numbered 1135..1391, all below the live range - remnants of an earlier log generation, carveable and invisible to any header-driven parse.

own/Shell Link (LNK, Unicode).tpl.notes: Authored fresh from MS-SHLLINK v20251121, section 2 read in full and closed at 23/23 units - not derived from any existing template, so it is ours to license. Verified on 4 samples from 4 different producing machines (3 plaso + 1 controlled shortcut): the declaration walk consumes each file EXACTLY, 0 bytes over or short, across every combination of optional structures present. Fixes both defects in the imported pair: timestamps are labelled Creation/ACCESS/WRITE at +28/+36/+44, and NAME_STRING is consumed first in StringData when HasName is set. Applies at the cursor rather than a fixed start, so it also works on a Shell Link embedded in another container such as a jump list stream. BOUNDED, not decoded: the LinkInfo body (VolumeID, LocalBasePath, CommonNetworkRelativeLink, CommonPathSuffix) and each ExtraData payload - the template language cannot follow an internal offset and return to a known position, so these are emitted as labelled hex with their offsets exposed. LinkFlags bits 9-12, 14-17, 19-25 steer behaviour rather than layout and are left in the raw value. LINKFLAGS UNKNOWN BITS (2026-08-25): the Windows SDK's ShlObj_core.h (10.0.19041, SHELL_LINK_DATA_FLAGS enum, read directly) names the two bits MS-SHLLINK leaves as Unused1/Unused2 - 0x800 is SLDF_HAS_LOGO3ID ('not used anymore', pre-Vista only) and 0x10000 is SLDF_FORCE_UNCNAME ('make GetPath() prefer the UNC name'). It also defines a 28th flag the spec draws as zero: 0x8000000 SLDF_PERSIST_VOLUME_ID_RELATIVE (Win8+), and a SetFlags() validity mask SLDF_VALID=0x0FFFF7FF that admits everything below bit 28 except 0x800. Corpus survey of 235 shell links on a Win11 26200 host (Recent, Start Menu, Desktop, Quick Launch, SendTo, plus 4 plaso samples; 36 distinct LinkFlags values): bits 11, 16 and 27 were set in 0/235, and bits 28-31 in 0/235. So the template's decision to leave those bits undecoded costs nothing on this corpus; bit 27 would be the first to add if a Win8+ producer path is ever seen to set it. The SLDF_VALID mask was NOT found as a 32-bit immediate (or its complement) in windows.storage.dll, shell32.dll, shlwapi.dll or SHCore.dll on this build, so whether current CShellLink::SetFlags still filters 0x800 is unverified; an IShellLinkDataList SetFlags/Save round-trip would settle it. REACTOS CROSS-CHECK (2026-08-25, CShellLink.cpp / shlobj.h / lnktool, read directly): (1) the SetFlags validity mask has a version history - Vista 0x003FF7FF, Win7 0x07FFF7FF, Win8+ 0x0FFFF7FF - and shlobj.h also names SLDF_RESERVED = 0x80000000 (bit 31). (2) ReactOS's SetFlags stores the value verbatim with NO SLDF_VALID masking, consistent with the mask not being found as an immediate in Windows binaries: it reads as a caller-side contract rather than an enforced filter. (3) Bit 11 SLDF_HAS_LOGO3ID was a live flag on 9x/NT4/2000/XP for 'Logo3' MSICD advertised shortcuts (IE4-era Internet Client SDK, blesslnk.exe); its data block has signature 0xA0000007 - the SAME value MS-SHLLINK and the current SDK assign to IconEnvironmentDataBlock - and the same 788-byte CHAR[260]+WCHAR[260] shape. So on a pre-Vista file with bit 11 set, an 0xA0000007 block is a Logo3 product identifier, not an icon path; the flag, not the signature, disambiguates. Not exercisable on the corpus to hand (0/235 have bit 11). PARSER LANDSCAPE for 0xA0000007 (checked 2026-08-25 in source): liblnk, Zimmerman Lnk, LnkParse3, 010 LNK.bt and ImHex all dispatch it unconditionally as IconEnvironmentDataBlock and none tests bit 11; Kaitai does not model ExtraData at all. Wine's shell32 does the reverse - it reads the block as the Logo3 product string when bit 11 is set, writes a product string under that same signature, and lists EXP_SZ_ICON_SIG as 'valid but unhandled', so Wine never sees an icon path there. Two live interpretations of one signature; only the flag tells them apart. SETFLAGS ROUND-TRIP (2026-08-25, Win11 26200, IShellLinkDataList via COM): bits 11, 28 and 31 are accepted by SetFlags (GetFlags returns them) but STRIPPED on Save; bits 16 and 27 persist to disk and survive reload. So the Win8 SLDF_VALID mask 0x0FFFF7FF is alive on this build and is enforced in the writer, not the setter - which is why it was never found near SetFlags. ESTABLISHED: bit 11 cannot be written by the Windows shell on 26200; a file with it set came from another producer or an older OS.

own/Shell Link (LNK, ANSI).tpl.notes: The IsUnicode-clear counterpart of own/Shell Link (LNK, Unicode).tpl, identical but for StringData reading single-byte code-page characters. UNTESTED: all 4 samples to hand have LinkFlags bit 7 set, so no non-Unicode shell link has exercised this variant. Promote once one is found - Windows has written Unicode links since at least Vista, so a genuine sample likely means a very old or hand-crafted file.

own/Shell Link TrackerDataBlock.tpl.notes: MS-SHLLINK 2.5.10, applied at the start of the 0xA0000003 ExtraData block. Verified on all 4 samples: BlockSize 0x60, signature 0xA0000003, Length 0x58, Version 0 in every one, and the 96-byte extent consumes the block exactly. Ground-truth checked on the controlled shortcut - MachineID decoded as 'vivo' against COMPUTERNAME=VIVO, and the DroidBirth file identifier's version-1 UUID node ec:91:61:9b:7d:6e resolves to a real adapter on that host (Bluetooth; the Wi-Fi NIC is ...7d:6d on the same combo chip). Note what that demonstrates: the node is NOT necessarily the primary or active adapter, so treat it as a lead identifying the machine rather than proof of a network path.

own/Shell Item - File Entry.tpl.notes: libyal libfwsi Windows Shell Item format v0.0.40, read to a declared scope and closed (9 units read, 9 classified out-of-scope). Community reverse engineering, not vendor documentation. Verified on 10 file-entry items from 3 shell links written on 3 machines (extension versions 8 and 9): the trailing first-extension-offset pointed at a 0xBEEF0004 block in 10/10, the walked long-name position equalled the declared offset in 10/10, the trailing copy equalled the first offset in 10/10, and every block ended exactly at the item end. The controlled shortcut's file entry returned the target's known creation/access/modification times to FAT's 2-second granularity. Not exercised: extension versions 3 and 7 (XP/2003, Vista), the localized-name tail, class flag 0x80, and the pre-XP layout, which is a different structure and out of scope.

own/Shell Item - Root Folder.tpl.notes: libyal libfwsi Windows Shell Item format v0.0.40, read to a declared scope and closed (9 units read, 9 classified out-of-scope). Community reverse engineering, not vendor documentation. Verified on 3 root items, all 20 bytes with sort index 0x50 and the My Computer / This PC CLSID. The optional extension block (size > 20) is bounded, not decoded, and was not seen.

own/Shell Item - Volume.tpl.notes: libyal libfwsi Windows Shell Item format v0.0.40, read to a declared scope and closed (9 units read, 9 classified out-of-scope). Community reverse engineering, not vendor documentation. Named form (flag 0x01) verified on 3 items, all 25 bytes for C:\. The unnamed GUID form, removable media flag, and the > 25-byte remainder (shell folder identifier / 0xbeef0025-27 extension) were not seen; the template's goto 25 for that remainder assumes the named form.

own/Shell Item - Envelope.tpl.notes: libyal libfwsi Windows Shell Item format v0.0.40, read to a declared scope and closed (9 units read, 9 classified out-of-scope). Community reverse engineering, not vendor documentation. Type dispatcher: size, class type nibble and flags, bounded payload, terminal-item guard. Exercised on all 16 items above.

own/Compound File Header.tpl.notes: Authored from MS-CFB v20200701 read for sections 2.1-2.6.3 (closed; 2.6.4-2.9 out of scope). Verified on 2 automaticDestinations-ms containers (plaso): signature, major 3 / minor 0x3E, byte order FFFE, sector shift 9, mini shift 6, cutoff 0x1000, first DIFAT FFFFFFFE, and file size = 512 + N*512 in both. The 109-entry DIFAT array is decoded; DIFAT sectors beyond it (files over 6.875 MB) are not needed for jump lists. Version 4 (4096-byte sector) files were not seen.

own/Compound File Directory Entry.tpl.notes: Authored from MS-CFB v20200701 read for sections 2.1-2.6.3 (closed; 2.6.4-2.9 out of scope). Verified by reading both containers' directories with the same field offsets (name length @64, type @66, start @116, size @120): root entry plus DestList and 3-11 numbered streams per file, every numbered stream beginning with a shell link header. Object types 2 and 5 seen; storages (type 1), red-black sibling traversal and CLSID/state/timestamps on storages were not exercised.

own/Jump List DestList Header.tpl.notes: Authored from libyal dtformats 'Jump lists format' read in full for the automatic and custom destinations sections (closed). Community reverse engineering; Microsoft has not published the DestList or custom destinations structures. Verified on a version 1 (Win7) and a version 3 (Win10) DestList: entry count matched the number of entries tiled (11 and 2), 'last entry number' equalled the highest entry number present, and the unknown at +12 decoded as a plausible float in both (22.4, 2.0), consistent with libyal's note. Version 4 not seen.

own/Jump List DestList Entry v1.tpl.notes: Authored from libyal dtformats 'Jump lists format' read in full for the automatic and custom destinations sections (closed). Community reverse engineering; Microsoft has not published the DestList or custom destinations structures. Verified on 11 entries from a Windows 7 DestList: the entries tiled the 2216-byte stream exactly at 114 + 2*chars each, hostname and FILETIME decoded sensibly, pin status -1 throughout, entry numbers 1-11 matched the container's stream names 1-b, and paths included both file paths and ::{CLSID} namespace items. Pinned entries (status >= 0) not seen.

own/Jump List DestList Entry v3.tpl.notes: Authored from libyal dtformats 'Jump lists format' read in full for the automatic and custom destinations sections (closed). Community reverse engineering; Microsoft has not published the DestList or custom destinations structures. Verified on 2 entries from a Windows 10 DestList: tiled the 584-byte stream exactly at 134 + 2*chars each, including the 4-byte trailer libyal marks as padding (zero in both). Hostname was empty for these URL entries; unknown@112 was FFFFFFFF and unknown@116 was 1 in both, matching libyal's 'status?' and 'access count?' guesses without confirming them. Only 2 entries and one producer build - promote the unknowns' names only with a larger corpus.

own/Jump List Custom Destinations.tpl.notes: Authored from libyal dtformats 'Jump lists format' read in full for the automatic and custom destinations sections (closed). Community reverse engineering; Microsoft has not published the DestList or custom destinations structures. Verified on 3 customDestinations-ms files: header version 2; category types 0, 1 and 2 all seen; every category footer BABFFBAB landed where predicted; 12 embedded shell links across the two non-empty files sized with the Shell Link template's walk consumed both files exactly (1775/1775, 17261/17261). The template decodes the header and first category only, because a shell link has no length field the template language can use to skip to the next category.
